entities.name: Quintus Aemilius Laetus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Quintus Aemilius Laetus, a Roman Praetorian Prefect, rose to prominence in the late 2nd century CE, serving Emperor Commodus before orchestrating his assassination in 192 CE. His actions directly plunged the Roman Empire into the tumultuous Year of the Five Emperors, a period of civil war and instability that fundamentally challenged the Principate and paved the way for the Severan dynasty. Laetus's career exemplifies the immense power wielded by the Praetorian Guard and its prefects in shaping imperial succession, often through violent means, during a critical juncture of Roman history.

Initially gaining Commodus's favor, Laetus was appointed Praetorian Prefect, one of the most powerful non-imperial positions in Rome, by 192 CE. As Commodus's increasingly erratic and tyrannical behavior alienated the Senate and the populace, Laetus, fearing for his own safety and political standing, conspired with the emperor's chamberlain Eclectus and mistress Marcia to eliminate him. On December 31, 192 CE, Commodus was strangled by a wrestler named Narcissus, likely at Laetus's instigation. Following the assassination, Laetus quickly installed Pertinax, an aged senator, as the new emperor, promising the Praetorians a substantial donative.

Laetus's role in Commodus's demise and the subsequent elevation of Pertinax directly triggered the "Year of the Five Emperors" (193 CE), a period of intense civil strife as various regional legions proclaimed their own candidates for the throne. His short-sighted plan to control the succession backfired when the Praetorian Guard, emboldened by their king-making power and dissatisfied with Pertinax, murdered the new emperor just 86 days into his reign. Laetus himself fell victim to the very instability he helped create, being executed by Pertinax's successor, Didius Julianus, who briefly bought the throne from the Praetorians, demonstrating the perilous nature of imperial politics and the fleeting loyalty of the Praetorian Guard.
